purpose: Compare temporal persistence of already-accepted high-altitude Rayleigh candidates across blocks without declaring either target scientifically supportable for productive KFS.

historical_stress_case_20241219nt.source: legacy observational audit empirical 20-minute candidate experiment
historical_stress_case_20241219nt.uncertainty_caveat: The historical experiment used temporal standard error from legacy corrected profiles and is not numerically equivalent to the current propagated Level 1 uncertainty model.

interpretation_notes: Candidate persistence is a diagnostic of temporal representativeness, not a productive KFS support flag.

For 20251107sapm, every current 20-minute block contains at least one shape-QA-accepted candidate at or above 15 km and 20 km for both 355 and 532 nm, although propagated SNR at those altitudes is weak.
For historical 20241219nt, only the first 20-minute block contains any accepted candidate at or above 15 km or 20 km; later blocks collapse to highest accepted altitudes near 6.4 and 5.5 km.
The contrast supports candidate-availability persistence as an auditable observable for future backbone design, but it does not define an acceptance fraction or threshold.
Numerical candidate counts between the two cases are not directly comparable because the historical uncertainty experiment differs from the current propagated uncertainty model.
